question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I first used broad searches for the style data, then switched to the vocabularies index when those searches returned no matches. The index exposed the choice and tier paths, so I requested both in the assigned HAL representation. The choice response supplied members, Boolean sets, map coverage, and conflict groups; the tier response supplied names and descriptions for the join. I read one full choice value to check that omission from a complete Boolean set meant false, and fetched the linked contract to see whether it added needed schema detail. Once the complete choice and tier lists supported the five matches and both groups, I had enough to answer; further individual value or tier reads would not add required facts.
